title: Scoped Session Proofing and Access Beacon: SCIM Reconciliation + Periodic Review Workflow
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Audit requests and external assessments increasingly require cryptographically verifiable snapshots showing who had access to tenant-scoped resources, when, and under what SSO assertion. Current systems produce CSV exports and ad-hoc SCIM delta logs that are hard to correlate with session tokens and RBAC bindings.

Objective: Build a lightweight 'Access Beacon' service that stitches together SSO/SAML assertions, SCIM provisioning events, RBAC role bindings, and session metadata to produce tamper-evident evidence bundles for periodic reviews and on-demand audits. The service should: (1) surface RBAC drift for tenants, (2) generate periodic attestation packages (signed), and (3) integrate with the Console to trigger reviewer workflows and with our evidence-retention pipeline for long-term storage (residency-aware).
acceptance_criteria: Access Beacon ingests SCIM user/group delta feed and SSO assertion logs for a tenant within 2 minutes of event arrival (best-effort).

For a given tenant and time window, Beacon can produce a signed evidence bundle with: list of active principals, role assignments, last login SAML assertion IDs, relevant session TTLs, and SCIM delta sequence covering the window.
Console UI: reviewer can kick off a 90-day periodic review job and receive a link to the generated evidence bundle and a reviewer checklist.
RBAC drift alerts generated when role membership changes exceed configured thresholds (default: 5 members changed in 24h) and recorded as review tasks in the cycle backlog.
Evidence bundles respect tenant residency/retention settings and are routed to the correct retention storage (S3 region or on-prem vault) based on tenant metadata.
End-to-end tests covering SCIM delta reconciliation, SSO log ingestion, signature verification, and reviewer flow exist and run in CI.
comments: 2025-02-16 - Marcus Li: Initial spike complete. Proof-of-concept can parse Okta SCIM delta events and normalize to canonical change records. Demo w/ staging tenant tomorrow.
2025-02-20 - PM review (Elena Rossi): Add explicit retention tie-in — reviewer bundles should record which retention policy was applied and include a retention-hash for downstream exports.
2025-02-24 - Design review (Priya Shah): Proposed reviewer checklist wireframes attached; prefer compact bundle view and copyable adjudication notes. UI acceptance criteria updated.

2025-02-28 - Marcus Li: Chose event-first approach (SCIM streaming) over nightly bulk reconciliation because onboarding latency is critical for enterprises with frequent HR-driven changes. Trade-off: extra complexity in deduplication and sequence gaps handling.

2025-03-03 - Security (Jared Nguyen): Requested threat model for signed bundles and key rotation plan. Decided to use a tenant-scoped signing key stored in KMS; rotation will publish new signing-keys and retain old keys for verification of historical bundles.
2025-03-04 - Marcus Li: Started implementation of the canonical change log (chanlog) + reconciliation worker. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2987
decision_log: Event-first ingestion chosen to reduce time-to-evidence for periodic reviews and on-demand requests; bulk reconciliation will remain as a backstop for out-of-order events.
Use tenant-scoped KMS keys to sign evidence bundles to limit blast radius and satisfy tenant-level auditors (vs single global key).
Retention-routing performed at bundle generation time to ensure bundles are stored in the correct residency jurisdiction and with the correct retention label.
mitigation_plan: If SCIM stream gap detected, trigger bulk reconcile for affected tenant window and annotate bundle with 'reconcile_performed: true'.
On signing key rotation, keep previous keys in verification list and publish mapping in bundle metadata so auditors can verify historical bundles.
Rate-limit generation jobs per-tenant to avoid overloaded storage writes; surface queue position to reviewer in Console.
notes: Integration targets: Okta SCIM and Azure AD SCIM connectors for provisioning; SAML/SSO assertion logs from our proxy and customer SAML IdP assertions when available.

Future work: wire evidence bundles into existing compliance exports for SOC2/ISO artifact assembly and provide an API for partners to request cryptographic proof-of-access without sharing raw exports.
Consider adding a small zero-knowledge component for tenant requests that want proof-of-membership without listing all user emails (policy dependent).
Estimated rollout: Beta for 3 pilot tenants in May 2025, GA in Q3 2025 pending legal sign-off.
